name: PlutoBook
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: HTML and CSS to PNG or PDF with no browser or JavaScript; Python wheel plutoprint
summary: C++ paged HTML and CSS layout engine with a Python wheel, plutoprint, that bundles it. It renders an HTML string or file to a PNG at a chosen pixel size, or to PDF, with flexbox, wrapped text and rounded corners; no browser, no script execution and no CSS gradients on the tested build.
use_when: Title cards, documents and text-heavy stills written as plain HTML and CSS, rendered without a browser
One PNG per frame where the page is a pure function of t and Chromium is unwanted
avoid_when: Pages that need JavaScript, CSS gradients or animation: playwright
JSX or React markup to SVG: satori; typeset documents from their own markup: typst

install.macos: python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install plutoprint==0.24.0

notes: 2026-11-27: the lead said plutoprint 0.23.0 and Homebrew PlutoBook 0.20.0; PyPI has plutoprint 0.24.0 (MIT, Python >=3.10, macOS arm64 wheel) bundling PlutoBook 0.21.0. The upstream library is MPL-2.0 per the lead (not re-checked); the wheel's own licence file is MIT.
2026-11-27: on the tested build a CSS linear-gradient or radial-gradient paints nothing (transparent), an unpainted background gives a transparent PNG, and inline <script> does not run.

assessment.rationale: PyPI plutoprint 0.24.0 uploaded 2026-11-27 with an arm64 macOS wheel that needs no system install; the upstream repository was pushed 2026-11-19. It renders real HTML and CSS to bitmaps natively; playwright needs Chromium, satori covers a JSX subset to SVG, typst has its own markup. Limits found: no gradients, no JavaScript.

evidence.result: 6 gating checks pass, repeat processes identical: HTML/CSS title card (flexbox, wrapped text, rounded box) renders to 1920x1080 PNG, 5 frames in shuffled order equal sequential, pixels match. Observed: CSS gradients paint nothing (transparent PNG), inline script does not run.
evidence.scope: Solid-colour HTML/CSS to PNG, one frame per t, macOS arm64, Python 3.12; the original gradient check failed; not PDF, web fonts, images, other OS or cross-machine hashes.
